They also give the 312 runners a comparison to last year.

agency:       The raw material is the organizers' own records: the registration export for the runner count, the donation ledger for the $11,400 total, and the sponsor and volunteer lists for exact names and spellings. The closest proxy is to keep every number to what the user stated, with no invented percentages or "last year" figures.

answers.plain:
Here's a draft you can paste in:

---

**Our Hope for Kids 5K was a huge success! 🎉🏃‍♀️🏃‍♂️**

This Saturday, **312 runners** laced up and showed up for kids, and together we raised **$11,400**! That's our biggest turnout yet, and well beyond last year. We're so grateful.

**Thank you to our sponsors** 💛
Your generosity made this day possible. Because of you, every dollar raised goes further for the kids we serve. We couldn't do this without your support.

**Thank you to our volunteers** 🙌
You were up early, out on the course, cheering at every turn, and making sure everything ran smoothly. You are the heart of this event.

**Thank you to the Ridgeview High cross-country team** 🏅
Your energy, encouragement, and support lifted every runner, from first-timers to seasoned racers. You set the tone for the whole morning, and we're proud to have you as part of our community.

And to every runner, walker, and cheerer: thank you for showing up for Hope for Kids. 💙

See you next year, and we're aiming even higher! 👟

#HopeForKids #HopeForKids5K #5K #CommunityRun #RidgeviewHigh #GiveBack #RunForACause

---

A few optional tweaks:
- **Tag sponsors**: add their handles (e.g., "Thanks to @sponsor1, @sponsor2...") for more reach and goodwill.
- **Add a number**: if you know last year's totals, something like "up from 200 runners last year" makes the growth concrete.
- **Say what the money does**: a line such as "$11,400 will provide ___ for local kids" is usually the most compelling part.

I can make it shorter, more casual, or tailor it with sponsor names if you share them.
answers.nudge:
# Instagram recap: Hope for Kids 5K

## Main caption (recommended)

**312 runners. $11,400 raised. One very loud Saturday. 🧡**

Because of you, the Hope for Kids 5K was our biggest one yet. We had more runners, more energy, and more money going to kids than ever before.

Some thank-yous:

**🏃 To our runners.** You ran, walked, jogged, and strolled. Some of you pushed strollers and some of you brought your dogs. Every one of you made this happen.

**🤝 To our sponsors.** [Sponsor 1], [Sponsor 2], [Sponsor 3], and [Sponsor 4]: you believed in this before race day, and that made it possible. Please support the businesses that support our community.

**🙌 To our volunteers.** You were up before sunrise to set up, direct traffic, hand out water, and cheer. You were the reason the day ran smoothly, and we couldn't have done it without you.

**🏅 To the @[RidgeviewXC handle] cross-country team.** Thank you for bringing your speed, your spirit, and your volume. You showed our younger runners what it looks like to love this sport.

Every dollar of the $11,400 goes toward [specific use, e.g., "school supplies, meals, and programs for local kids"]. That's real impact, and you did it by lacing up on a Saturday morning.

Save the date for next year: [date or "details coming soon"]. 👟

Tag yourself and your people in the comments. We want to see your finish-line photos! 📸

#HopeForKids5K #[YourCity]Running #5KForACause #CommunityRuns #RidgeviewXC #GiveBack

---

## Shorter version (if you want a punchier caption)

**312 runners. $11,400. Our biggest Hope for Kids 5K ever.** 🧡

Thank you to our sponsors [@tags] for backing us, our volunteers for making race day run smoothly, and the @[RidgeviewXC] team for bringing the speed and the spirit.

Every dollar goes to [cause]. You showed up for kids, and it mattered.

See you next year! 👟

---

## Carousel plan (posts with a carousel usually get more engagement)

1. **Cover:** your best action shot, such as the start line or finish-line energy. Overlay text: "312 runners. $11,400. Thank you."
2. **Big numbers graphic:** "312 runners / $11,400 raised / our biggest year yet"
3. **Sponsor slide:** all logos on one clean graphic. Tag them in the photo and the caption.
4. **Volunteers:** a group photo or candid shot at the water station.
5. **Ridgeview XC team:** a photo of them at the start, finish, or cheering.
6. **Closing slide:** "See you next year" with the date, if you have it.

## Posting tips
- **Tag everyone.** Sponsors, the school, and the XC team will likely reshare, which expands your reach.
- **Pin a comment** with the donation link, in case anyone missed the chance to give.
- **Post a Story** with a "Tag your finish photo" sticker, and reshare the tagged posts.
- **Post within a day or two**, while people are still talking about it. Mornings or early evenings usually work well.

## Before you post
- **Fill in the placeholders:** sponsor names and handles, the Ridgeview handle, what the funds support, and next year's date.
- **Check the claim:** I wrote "biggest yet" because you said it was way more than last year. If you have last year's numbers, something like "up from [X] last year" is stronger.
- **Check photo permissions** for any identifiable minors, especially the high school runners.

If you send me the sponsor list, the cause the money supports, and the tone you want (more playful or more heartfelt), I can tailor the final version.
